item.title: Cross-Domain Channel Estimation for MU-MIMO-OFDM
item.description: arXiv:2611.10052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional channel estimation for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) relies on the pilot interpolation without explicitly identifying the sparse delay-angle (DA) components. To exploit DA sparsity while maintaining backward compatibility with existing MIMO-OFDM systems, we propose a cross-domain channel estimation scheme for multiuser MIMO-OFDM (MU-MIMO-OFDM) systems. The scheme exploits the circular convolution structure in the DA domain to identify candidate DA pairs by correlating delay-domain observations with DA pilot responses. These pairs and the known pilots then define a time-frequency (TF) dictionary for refining the DA coefficients from TF observations through least-squares or sparsity-regularized fitting. The refined coefficients and candidate pairs reconstruct the aggregate channel across antennas and subcarriers aligning with the geometric channel model. Numerical results show approximately 10 dB and 7 dB lower normalized mean-square error than the conventional OFDM estimation schemes for integer and fractional delay and angle indices, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Mingcheng Nie, Shuangyang Li, Ruoxi Chong, Giuseppe Caire, Yonghui Li

item.title: On Relative Greedy Weights
item.description: arXiv:2611.10567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Relative greedy weights were introduced by Li and Liu in [19] as a measure of information leakage in coordinated two-party wire-tap channels of type II when the adversary follows a greedy strategy. Their definition can be viewed as a relative version of the CEZ greedy weights, which are only locally greedy. In this paper, we revisit the concept of greediness and relative greediness introducing new measures, and we discuss other perhaps more relevant applications of relative greedy weights than the coordinated two-party wire-tap channel of type II. We pay special attention to bottom-up greedy weights, which correspond to an adversary with an ultimate greedy approach, and we present families of nested codes for which such weights are larger than the relative CEZ greedy weights.
item.dc:creator: Olav Geil

item.title: Learning-Assisted Beamforming Optimization for Hybrid XL-RIS-Aided Communication
item.description: arXiv:2611.10569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid active-passive extremely large-scale reconfigurable intelligent surface (XL-RIS) architectures mitigate the double-hop path loss of passive RIS while enabling near-field spatial energy focusing, but impose a computationally intensive mixed discrete-continuous beamforming design problem under strict radio-frequency (RF) power constraints. This paper investigates a hybrid XL-RIS-assisted downlink multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) system in the near-field regime. The joint optimization of the base station (BS) precoder, discrete XL-RIS phase shifts, and active-element amplification gains is addressed via a discrete coordinate ascent (DCA)-based alternating optimization (AO) framework, in which discrete variables are updated through local index-domain searches and the BS precoder is derived in closed form via a noise-aware minimum mean-square error (MMSE) criterion. To reduce the per-sample computational cost for XL-RIS apertures, a deep unfolding (DU) framework is proposed as a low-complexity alternative, unrolling a fixed number of Riemannian gradient ascent steps on the sum-rate objective and recovering the discrete phase configuration via quantized phasor projection, with one learnable step size per layer trained in a self-supervised manner. Numerical results under near-field spherical-wave channel models confirm that the DU framework achieves sum-rate performance close to the AO scheme with substantially lower and nearly constant runtime, and that both schemes consistently outperform manifold optimization under discrete hardware constraints.
item.dc:creator: Awuni Mohammed Abdul-Razak, Kyungchun Lee

item.title: Performance Analysis of Entanglement Swapping DV-QKD over MIMO FSO Channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.10743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) free-space optical (FSO) quantum communication systems employing polarization-encoded discrete-variable quantum key distribution (DV-QKD), based on entanglement swapping, with the goal of extending secure communications beyond the reach of a direct link. The FSO channels are subject to atmospheric absorption, diffraction, beam wander, pointing errors, and turbulence-induced fading, while background noise and detector imperfections degrade the performance. An eavesdropper controlling the channels and the relay is also considered. To analyze the performance of the considered system, both hops MIMO channels are decomposed into parallel spatial eigenchannels via singular value decomposition (SVD), photon loss is modeled using Kraus operators, and a threshold-detector model is developed for the relay. Based on these models, closed-form per-eigenchannel expressions for the relay gain are derived, which are then used to obtain expressions for the quantum bit error rate (QBER) and the secret key rate (SKR). Numerical results demonstrate that entanglement swapping maintains a low QBER over longer distances than direct transmission, extending the communication range beyond the noise-limited cutoff of the direct link, at the cost of a lower SKR at short distances. The crossover distance beyond which entanglement swapping prevails is determined mainly by the background noise and the detector technology, and it is demonstrated to increase with MIMO configurations. Moreover, the reach gain is shown to be maximized for a midpoint relay. Finally, since each swapping event requires a single-pair emission from both sources, a near-deterministic entangled-photon source is required, which spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources do not provide at practical key rates, whereas MIMO substantially relaxes this requirement.
item.dc:creator: Sushil Kumar, Soumya P. Dash, George C. Alexandropoulos

item.title: New Classes of CCZ-Inequivalent APN Functions with Boomerang Uniformity One in Odd Characteristic: Differential and Boomerang Spectra
item.description: arXiv:2611.10766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $q=p^n>3$ be an odd prime power and let $g:\F_q\to\F_q$ be an even perfect nonlinear (PN) function with $g(0)=0$. We construct almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions $G_{\lambda,M}(x)=g(x)+M(x)+\lambda(x^{q-1}-1)$, where $\lambda\in\F_q^*$, $-\lambda\notin g(\F_q)$, and $M$ is an $\F_p$-linearized permutation polynomial. These one-point modifications of $g+M$ have boomerang uniformity one, the smallest possible value for APN functions in odd characteristic. We give complete differential and boomerang spectrum formulas and obtain closed-form evaluations for selected constructions based on Coulter--Matthews monomials and Dembowski--Ostrom polynomials. For $q>7$, comparison of differential spectra establishes CCZ-inequivalence to all APN monomial families listed in the paper and every APN binomial in the original Ness--Helleseth family or its extension by Zeng et al. We characterize CCZ-equivalence within our construction, showing that any two linearly inequivalent even PN functions over the same field yield CCZ-inequivalent APN functions. We obtain three pairwise CCZ-inequivalent APN functions with boomerang uniformity one over $\F_{p^{15\ell}}$ for every $\ell\ge1$, six over $\F_{p^{120r}}$ for every $r\ge1$, and unbounded numbers of such classes in characteristic three. We further prove that CCZ-equivalence and EA-equivalence coincide for functions at Hamming distance at most $m$ from a PN function, provided that $m(m+1)<q-q/p$. We also show that all our APN functions have the maximal possible algebraic degree $n(p-1)$. Finally, we exhibit both CCZ-equivalent and CCZ-inequivalent APN pairs with boomerang uniformity one at Hamming distance one.
item.dc:creator: Namhun Koo, Soonhak Kwon

item.title: BP-based qLDPC Decoding under Long-range Correlated Noise: Trapping Configurations and Prior Mismatch
item.description: arXiv:2611.10796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the robustness of two state-of-the-art BP-based qLDPC decoders, Relay-BP and beam search, designed for independent noise when applied to spatially correlated noise with unchanged single-mechanism error probabilities. We generate correlated errors with a hidden Gaussian Markov random field, which lets us control the strength and range of the correlation while keeping every marginal error probability exact. This setting complements correlation-aware decoding: it asks how existing decoders perform when their assumed joint error model is mismatched. Across multiple tested circuits and code instances that we simulated, we observe that correlations can change logical error rates by orders of magnitude, reduce the finite-size distance advantage, and alter the relative ranking of Relay-BP, beam search, and BP-OSD. On one of the two tested circuits, Relay-BP and beam search become worse than BP-OSD, and increasing relay memory or beam width does not compensate for the degradation. Configuration analysis indicates that correlation primarily increases the probability of trapping configurations that are known to challenge these decoders; at matched error weight, correlated errors still cause decoding failures several times more often than i.i.d. errors. Finally, supplying the decoders with the marginals conditioned on the hidden field recovers most of the lost performance in the tested settings identifying prior mismatch as a major contributor to performance degradation under correlation.
item.dc:creator: Abhinav Dangi, Avhishek Chatterjee

item.title: Quantum channel bounds for constant-composition codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.10827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the quantum-channel optimization of Alrabiah and Guruswami to $q$-ary constant-composition codes. We study explicit channel and flag constructions that recover selected classical asymptotic upper bounds, including the Ben-Haim--Litsyn, moving-subspace and Horn-channel bounds. We give two equivalent formulations, Gram and flag, and prove stability of the obtained upper bounds under permutation transport and generalized shortening. A hierarchy defined by bounding the output-state ranks within each flag improves strictly between consecutive levels at every composition and every positive distance below the Plotkin threshold. We provide finite matrix parametrizations of these bounds (i.e., the number of variables does not depend on the length of codes under consideration). Numerical optimization rapidly produces improvements over the known asymptotic upper bounds throughout all tested nonbinary parameter ranges. For rational input data, each finite level admits near-optimal feasible rational descriptions of polynomial length. Their feasibility can be checked exactly and their objective values computed to any prescribed accuracy in polynomial time; the associated threshold problem with a prescribed gap belongs to $\mathsf{PromiseNP}$.
item.dc:creator: Artur Akhiiarov, Peter Boyvalenkov, Danila Cherkashin, Andrei Raigorodskii

item.title: Efficient SC-Flip Decoding for Polar Codes through Decision-Boundary Normalization
item.description: arXiv:2611.10846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate first erroneous position (FEP) identification is key to improving the error-correction performance of successive cancellation flip (SCF) decoding. However, FEP identification remains challenging with a limited number of re-decoding attempts. To address this issue, we propose decision-boundary normalization (DBN) to improve FEP identification and develop a novel DBN-SCF decoding algorithm. DBN normalizes the magnitude of each decision log-likelihood ratio (LLR) by the standard deviation predicted by the Gaussian approximation (GA) for the corresponding bit-channel. This allows a single normalized threshold to be shared across bit-channels within each code configuration, giving it a consistent statistical meaning and avoiding per-channel calibration. DBN-SCF decoding selects candidate flip positions from the information set in the natural successive cancellation (SC) decoding order using a threshold, without sorting. Moreover, DBN-SCF decoding achieves better error-correction performance with a limited number of re-decoding attempts. It also requires lower average decoding complexity than existing SCF decoding methods at a comparable level of error-correction performance.
item.dc:creator: Gulinisha Yiming, Zhongjun Yang, Zhicheng Liu, Zhiming Ma, Xumin Ni, Yuting Liu

item.title: Quantum synchronizable codes, polynomial and quasi-polynomial shifts
item.description: arXiv:2611.10903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum synchronizable codes protect quantum information against Pauli errors and against misalignments of the block boundaries. Almost all known constructions use cyclic codes, because the channel shifts the transmitted block cyclically. We study what happens when the algebraic shift of the code differs from the physical one. When one uses a twisted padding, constacyclic codes synchronize at no cost, and they are the only polycyclic codes with this property for a linear padding. For the other polycyclic codes, we measure the cost of each misaligned position, and we show that the phase damage it causes can be corrected as erasures. Using annihilator duality, we extend the construction to quasi-polycyclic codes, in which the cost is confined to a single block. We prove that the usual quasi-cyclic families have a distance bound that does not grow with the length, and show that quasi-polycyclic codes over repeated-root trinomials overcome it, giving synchronizable codes with larger dimension and distance than the known synchronizable codes of the same length.
item.dc:creator: Edgar Mart\'inez-Moro, Miguel de los R\'ios de Antonio

item.title: Optimal Sampling and Transmission Policy for Information Freshness in Gossip Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.10952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the optimal sampling and transmission policies for a transmitter communicating with n gossiping receivers with the objective of tracking a source's status over time using a semantic freshness metric: Version Age of Information (VAoI). The transmitter observes the version changes in the source, and can acquire a new information version by paying a sampling cost. The receivers gossip, allowing information exchange among each other without direct transmission. Gossiping can save on transmission cost, but it may propagate stale version information, necessitating transmitter intervention. With imperfect communication links, we formulate an infinite horizon average cost Markov Decision Process (MDP) in order to jointly optimize receivers' VAoIs, sampling and transmission costs in a time slotted fully connected (FC) gossip network. We first solve the MDP using Relative Value Iteration (RVI) algorithm. Then, we prove that the sampling decision has a threshold structure in the transmitter VAoI. Further, under reliable gossiping links, we show that transmission and idling has an VAoI-difference threshold structure with minimum VAoI activation. Numerical results obtained using RVI show that the optimal policy consistently outperforms natural baselines. These results characterize how source sampling, direct transmission, and receiver gossip should be jointly coordinated for cost-aware semantic freshness in gossip networks.
item.dc:creator: Irtiza Hasan, Ahmed Arafa

item.title: Iterative Interference Cancellation for Near-Field XL-MIMO Networks with LoS Channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.11038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In extra-large multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems, near-field users experience spherical wavefront propagation, offering higher spatial resolution than far-field plane-wave models, but complicating signal detection and interference cancellation. Under line-of-sight conditions, we propose a weighted-rate successive interference cancellation (WR-SIC) scheme whose ordering metric exploits the enhanced spatial degrees of freedom of near-field propagation to prioritize users with stronger channels. An iterative detection and decoding (IDD) scheme with LDPC coding is then developed. Simulations in hybrid near- and far-field deployments show that the proposed WR-SIC and IDD schemes improve bit-error and sum rates over existing schemes
item.dc:creator: Nayyab Haider, Rodrigo C. de Lamare

item.title: QoS-Aware Energy-Efficient Sub-THz Near-Field Multiuser Hybrid MIMO Systems Employing Circular Arrays
item.description: arXiv:2611.11097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near-field communications have emerged as a promising technology for future sixth-generation (6G) networks. However, designing energy-efficient hybrid beamfocusing schemes for multiuser (MU) systems remains challenging due to the non-convex quality-of-service (QoS) constraints and hardware limitations of hybrid architectures. In this paper, we investigate a hybrid massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) architecture for a near-field sub-THz MU downlink system employing a large uniform circular array (UCA) at the base station. A QoS-aware transmit power minimization problem is formulated for energy-efficient beamfocusing and addressed through a two-stage penalty-driven joint optimization (PDJO) framework, where auxiliary variables are introduced to reformulate the QoS constraints into second-order cone (SOC) constraints. Furthermore, a near-field polar-domain codebook is developed via joint angle- and distance-domain sampling. We establish that the fully digital (FD) beamfocuser lies within the column space of the proposed codebook, enabling hybrid precoder design to be formulated as a multiple measurement vector (MMV)-based sparse approximation problem. The formulated problem is then solved using a low-complexity simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit (SOMP) algorithm under hardware and transmit power constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves spectral- and energy-efficiency performance close to the ideal FD beamfocusing scheme while providing a favorable trade-off between hardware complexity and system performance.
item.dc:creator: Priya Gupta, Prabhanshu Yadav, Suraj Srivastava

item.title: A Characterization of $q$-Ary $2$-Designs and a $3$-Design Obstruction for Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.11219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}_k$ be the doubly extended Reed--Solomon code with parameters $[q+1,k,q-k+2]_q$, where $q\ge3$ is a prime power and $2\le k\le q$. We prove a conjecture of Wu and Zhou by showing that the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_k$ do not form a $q$-ary $3$-design when $2\le k\le q-1$. Using shortening, we extend this obstruction to every nonempty weight class with $3\le w<q+1$. We also establish that each individual nonempty positive-weight class of $\mathcal{C}_k$ forms a $q$-ary $2$-design if and only if $\gcd(k-1,q-1)=1$. Consequently, every nonempty positive-weight class below full support has exact $q$-ary design strength $2$ when this coprimality condition holds, and $1$ otherwise.The three-design obstruction follows by applying a classical subset-product character identity to a marginal covering count for three prescribed nonzero symbols. The comparison between weights rests on a covering-count formulation of the classical MDS coset-weight relations. For every linear $[n,k,d]_q$ MDS code with $2\le k\le n-1$, this formulation shows that the $q$-ary $2$-design property at any one nonempty positive weight is equivalent to the same property at every nonempty positive weight.More generally, for $2\le t\le\min\{k,d\}$, we prove that the $q$-ary $t$-design property at any $t-1$ distinct nonempty positive weights forces it at all nonempty positive weights.
item.dc:creator: Guanghui Zhang, Zhengbang Zha

item.title: Beating the Probabilistic Bound for Hashing and Improving Lower Bounds for Trifferent Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.11262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We improve the probabilistic lower bounds on the rates of hash codes and list-recoverable codes. For perfect $q$-hashing, we prove $R_q>B_q$ for every $q\geq 3$. Our main result concerns non-perfect hashing. For every $q\geq 4$, we prove $R_{q,3}>B_{q,3}+\frac{1}{250000}.$ In particular, the case $q=9$, combined with the Tetra code, strictly improves the K\"orner-Marton lower bound $R_3\geq \frac14\log(9/5)$ for trifferent codes. We also extend the method to $(p,2,3)$-list recovery. For every $q\geq 4$ and $0\leq p<\frac{q-2}{12(q-1)}$, we prove $R_q^{\mathrm{LR}}(p)>B_q^{\mathrm{LR}}(p)$. For every fixed $0\leq p<1/18$, the rate improvement is bounded below by a positive constant independent of $q\geq 4$. The same holds for every fixed $0\le p<1/12$ when $q$ is sufficiently large.
item.dc:creator: Chen Yuan, Ruiqi Zhu

item.title: Joint Design of Communication and Control in Center-Fed Pinching-Antenna Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.11412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An analytical and optimization framework for the joint design of communication and control (JDCC) in a center-fed pinching-antenna system (C-PASS) is proposed. Within this framework, the mathematical coupling between data throughput and closed-loop control cost is characterized for JDCC. The analysis captures the mutual interference between concurrently transmitted data and control streams during uplink state uploading and downlink command delivery. Based on this coupling, an achievable communication-control performance region is established for C-PASS. Accordingly, a throughput maximization problem is formulated to jointly optimize digital and pinching beamforming subject to control-cost constraints. To address this problem, an alternating optimization algorithm is developed based on constraint reformulation and resource decomposition. The proposed framework reveals how control requirements shape achievable data throughput, guiding the joint beamforming design. Numerical results demonstrate that 1) the proposed C-PASS design achieves 110.2\% higher frame-average throughput than conventional PASS, and 2) the proposed concurrent data-control transmission protocol increases frame-average throughput by up to 66.7\% over separated transmission.
item.dc:creator: Xu Gan, Yuanwei Liu, Hyundong Shin

item.title: Sharp Rates for Optimal Recovery of Bandlimited Functions from Localized Oversampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.11461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is well-known that one can recover a function $f$ bandlimited to $[-\delta,\delta]$ ( $0<\delta<\pi$) from its finite sample data $f(j),-n\le j\le n$, with an approximation error exponentially decaying to zero as $n$ tends to infinity. Various regularized Shannon sampling formula have been proposed to achieve such exponential approximation. So far the best rate has been $$ O\biggl(\frac1{\sqrt{n}}\exp(-(\pi-\delta)n)\biggr). $$ We establish that the optimal recovery algorithm in the worst-case scenario achieves an approximation error $\rho_{n,\delta}$ satisfying $$ c_* \frac1{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\frac\delta 4)^{2n+1/2}\le \rho_{n,\delta}\le C^* \frac1{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\frac\delta 4)^{2n+1/2}, \quad 0<\delta\leq\pi,\quad n\geq1, $$ where $c_*,C^*$ are positive constants independent of $n$ and $\delta$. This result identifies the best possible exponential rate to reconstruct bandlimited functions from two-sided finite oversampling data. In other words, $$ \rho_{n,\delta} \asymp \frac{\tan\frac\delta 4}{\sqrt{n}}\exp\bigl(-c_\delta(\pi-\delta)n\bigr), $$ where $c_\delta$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,\pi]$ and $$ \lim_{\delta\to\pi^-}c_\delta=1,\ \lim_{\delta\to 0^+}c_\delta=+\infty. $$ We also make the new finding that one can also reconstruct $f$ bandlimited to $[-\delta,\delta]$ with exponentially decaying error from one-sided sample data $f(j)$, $1\le j\le n$, and the sharp rate of approximation error $\rho_{n,\delta}'$ of the optimal algorithm is $$ \rho_{n,\delta}' \asymp \sqrt{\delta/\pi}\sin^n(\delta/2). $$
item.dc:creator: Wentao Huang, Haizhang Zhang

item.title: Compression of Sources with Memory and Private Random Access
item.description: arXiv:2611.11501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Private local decoding imposes a stringent constraint on compression: the codeword bits used to recover a source symbol must reveal nothing about the remaining symbols beyond what the recovered symbol itself reveals. For memoryless sources, this constraint is known to be compatible with entropy-rate compression. We show that the same holds for any stationary ergodic source over a finite alphabet. Specifically, every rate above the entropy rate is achievable with exact privacy and error-free local decoding on a set of source sequences whose probability tends to one. In contrast, we exhibit non-ergodic sources for which private local decoding incurs a strictly positive rate penalty.
item.dc:creator: Venkat Chandar, Aslan Tchamkerten, Shashank Vatedka

item.title: Binary Belief Propagation Fixed Points: Finiteness, Rigidity, and Topological Complexity
item.description: arXiv:2611.11713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A fixed finite binary Ising model has only finitely many admissible complex belief propagation fixed points, even at degenerate parameter values. Families of positive fixed points obtained by varying external fields can nevertheless have nontrivial topology. We study this distinction through the external-field projection. For a fixed field, we prove finiteness by bounding the pole orders of the magnetizations on a hypothetical complex solution curve. The generic degree on the support graph then bounds the total local multiplicity. A graph has a single smooth real line as its full positive response for every choice of positive couplings, base field, and strictly positive sweep direction exactly when it contains no two vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of cycle rank at least two. Two such subgraphs suffice to create a circular component. For a plane obtained by varying two vertex fields, connected simple bipartite cubic graphs with one uniform coupling and a universal bound on the fixed fields realize every genus. The minimum number of vertices grows logarithmically in the genus, by a matching algebraic upper bound on Betti numbers. Finally, we certify the complete field discriminant of an eighteen-vertex product model and recover its torus component's genus from the counts of distinct roots on all field cells. The three main theorems, including the logarithmic size bounds, are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Watanabe

item.title: Bounds and Constructions for Optimal Wide-Gap Frequency Hopping Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2611.11747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a frequency-hopping (FH) system, to reduce interference to the received signal, each user's frequency hopping sequence (FHS) shall have wide-gap property. In this paper, we update the upper bounds on the minimum gaps of optimal uniform wide-gap frequency hopping sequences (WGFHS) with parameters $(v,s,\lambda;e)$ where $v=ks, k\ge 3, \lambda=k$ and $s\ge k(k-1)+1$ is odd. We completely prove the existence of such WGFHSs for $k\le 3$.
item.dc:creator: Jiwen Zhang, Haitao Cao

item.title: Joint LSFC and Nakagami-m Estimation From Downlink SINR in GZF-Precoded CF-mMIMO
item.description: arXiv:2611.11849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate characterization of the instantaneous signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) is important for reliability-sensitive cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) systems. This paper proposes a joint estimation method for link-specific large-scale fading coefficients (LSFCs) and a common Nakagami-$m$ shape parameter using power and downlink SINR measurements. A tractable SINR distribution is first derived under global zero-forcing (GZF) precoding, Nakagami-$m$ fading, and link-level fractional power control (FPC). Based on the derived probability density function (PDF), a model-driven neural network (NN) is developed to solve the resulting maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) problem. Simulations show that the reconstructed SINR distributions obtained with the estimated parameters closely match the empirical distributions. With $2 \times 10^{5}$ samples, the proposed method achieves an LSFC root-mean-square error (RMSE) of approximately 1.0 dB and an $m$ RMSE of approximately 0.085.
item.dc:creator: Longfei Liu, Yichen Guo, Lili Xu, Yihang Cheng, Tao Peng, Wenbo Wang

item.title: Mitigating the BICM Loss in MIMO Receivers with Correlation-Informed Logits
item.description: arXiv:2611.12223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bit-interleaved coded modulation (BICM) is widely used in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless systems. However, separating MIMO data detection from channel decoding and only exchanging per-bit soft information discards correlation information among the bits within each transmit vector. We show that the resulting information loss limits the performance of practical one-shot receivers. Even though iterative detection and decoding (IDD) can recover most of this loss, IDD significantly increases receiver complexity and latency. In order to reduce this loss, we propose COrrelation-Informed Logits (COIL), a soft-output format that combines per-bit soft information with pairwise coupling logits for correlated bits. We show how to incorporate these coupling logits into a conventional belief-propagation-based channel decoder, which enables correlation-aware decoding in a one-shot receiver without IDD. We evaluate COIL in a MIMO-BICM system with a conventional low-density parity-check code. For a 4x4 MIMO orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system, a one-shot linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receiver with COIL outperforms a conventional one-shot unbiased LMMSE receiver by 1.3dB and operates within 0.8dB of four-iteration IDD, while requiring only a single pass through the data detector.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Studer

item.title: Fundamental Outage and Diversity Limits of Fluid Antenna Multiple Access Under Correlated Nakagami-$m$ Fading
item.description: arXiv:2611.12247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing analytical studies of fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA) are largely confined to Rayleigh fading, independent-port assumptions, or asymptotic selection metrics, leaving the fundamental outage behavior under realistic fading and spatial correlation conditions uncharacterized. This paper fills this gap by presenting the first exact and asymptotically tight outage analysis of interference-limited FAMA systems under spatially correlated Nakagami-$m$ fading. By explicitly modeling the joint statistics of the desired and interference powers across fluid-antenna ports, \textcolor{black}{we first formulate the outage probability in terms of the joint desired-signal and interference distributions and then derive an explicit integral expression under a tractable single-reference-port spatial correlation model.} Building on this result, we establish a rigorous diversity-order characterization revealing that the achievable diversity is jointly dictated by the fading severity and the spatial correlation rank imposed by the finite antenna aperture, rather than by the nominal number of ports. To enable accurate and tractable performance evaluation beyond the asymptotic regime, we further introduce a Gamma-matched outage approximation that preserves both the exact diversity order and the array-gain constant. The resulting closed-form expression provides an accurate characterization over a wide range of signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) thresholds and offers clear physical insight into the role of spatial correlation in FAMA systems. Extensive Monte Carlo (MC) simulations confirm the tightness of the exact analysis, the sharpness of the asymptotic results, and the accuracy of the proposed approximation.
item.dc:creator: Anastasios Papazafeiropoulos

item.title: Reference-Dependent Utility Optimization for Goal-Oriented Communication Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.12480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traditional communication resource allocation optimizes operational metrics such as rate, latency, energy efficiency, and reliability. Motivated by goal-oriented semantic communication, we develop a generalized allocation framework that transforms operational rewards through reference-dependent user utilities and evaluates them via expected utility, cumulative prospect theory (CPT), or related decision criteria. The formulation separates operational rewards, user-side valuations, and system-level decision criteria under uncertainty. We characterize utilities incorporating QoS/service reference levels, deficit sensitivity, post-reference saturation, and loss aversion. Weighted sum-reward maximization, proportional fairness, $\alpha$-fairness, and stochastic expected utility maximization emerge as exact special cases, while soft QoS-aware allocation follows from a deficit-penalty generalization. For deterministic orthogonal systems, we derive utility-weighted marginal-reward KKT conditions characterizing global optimality under concave composite objectives. For nonorthogonal and stochastic systems, we develop successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithms and establish stationary-point guarantees under explicit smooth and composite nonsmooth assumptions, including a CPT branch-stationarity result under eventual nondegenerate ordering identification. For globally solved penalized problems, we derive an $O(1/\lambda)$ bound on excess aggregate soft-QoS deficit, and on the deficit itself whenever a QoS-feasible allocation exists. Additionally, we establish an $O(1/\epsilon^2)$ outer iteration bound for the smooth fixed-step SCA best-response residual. Numerical examples demonstrate how reference points, marginal utility slopes, channel quality, and resource budgets influence active users and allocation policies.
item.dc:creator: Symeon Vaidanis, Photios A. Stavrou, Marios Kountouris

item.title: Fresh Enough to Decide: Age of Intelligence for Cost-Aware Model Synchronization in Dynamic IoT Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.09935v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Resource-constrained IoT devices cache learned models for real-time decisions, but frequent updates incur substantial bandwidth, energy, and service overhead. Because decision-relevant model differences need not grow with elapsed time, we define Age of Intelligence (AoInt) as a model-version-relative, client-specific, and action utility distortion, and formulate synchronization as a tradeoff between stale-decision regret and refresh cost. Furthermore, we develop Kullback-Leibler-aware AoInt Synchronization (KL-AoIntSync), which accumulates output-distribution changes using client-specific unlabeled probes, whereas Parameter-aware AoInt Synchronization (Param-AoIntSync) uses a server-broadcast scalar parameter change. Then, we establish pathwise guarantees with fixed client distributions, action sets, and utilities. The numerical results show that calibrated Param-AoIntSync reduces joint synchronization cost by 6.15% relative to an Instant-Parameters policy while performing comparably to KL-AoIntSync.
item.dc:creator: Hui Wang, Seyyedali Hosseinalipour, Jacob Chakareski, Ming Shi

item.title: Topology and Information in Regularized Transport on Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.09968v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how two geometries of mass on a finite graph interact: the information geometry of the generalized entropy $F_q$ used for regularized transport, and the arithmetic of divisors governed by the Riemann--Roch theorem of Baker and Norine and by the Jacobian. Because the correction term of $F_q$ is affine, $F_q$-regularization at strength $\gamma$ is Tsallis regularization at temperature $\gamma/q$. Over the reals, chip-firing connects all configurations of equal degree, so the Jacobian enters transport only through integrality. We introduce the transport defect, the worst-case cost of steering $d$ chips towards a target by chip-firing, and prove $1/d\le\delta_{\TV}(D)\le(d-r(D))/d=(g-1-r(K-D))/d\le\min(1,g/d)$ whenever $g\ge1$; vertex multiplicities give a lower bound and an equality criterion. A regularized topological gap $\Gamma_{q,\gamma}(D,E)$ tends to the chip-move defect as $\gamma\to0$, lies in an explicit window, has a high-temperature slope given by Tsallis coupling entropies, and admits a positive regime if and only if $g\ge1$. Dual potentials certify exactly the convex relaxation of a linear system; the remainder is an integrality gap. Zeros in optimal plans occur only for $q>1$, by a mechanism different from the sign change of $\Gamma$. Exact computations on $1784$ divisor classes find the rank bound $(d-r(D))/d$ attained in $1769$ of them, an observed frequency. Experiments on honeycomb and Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi networks with $10^2$ to $10^5$ nodes test the statements on regularized plans, not $\Gamma$; over $10^3\le n\le10^5$ their transport costs are consistent with growth like $n^{1/2}$ and $\log n$, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Shintaro Yoshizawa

item.title: Testing CCZ-equivalence to permutations via projections of Walsh zero spaces, with applications to APN functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.10269v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Whether almost perfect nonlinear (APN) permutations exist in even dimension $n\ge 8$ is a long-standing open question, the big APN problem. The only example known in even dimension, on six bits, was found from a quadratic APN function that is not itself a permutation, by Carlet--Charpin--Zinoviev (CCZ) equivalence. It is therefore natural to test APN functions for CCZ-equivalence to a permutation. This amounts to finding two complementary $n$-dimensional subspaces among the zeros of the Walsh transform, which lie in $\mathbb{F}_2^{2n}$. A known necessary condition only uses their projections to $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and cannot decide every case. We give an exact test for functions whose Walsh supports are affine, including all quadratic functions. It reconstructs the subspaces from their projections, through searches for subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and for constrained bilinear maps. On the benchmarked functions in dimension twelve, it lists them $39$ to $55$ times faster than the generic search of the commonly used sboxU library. We then study the functions $x^3+a^{-1}\mathrm{Tr}(a^3x^9)$, which G\"olo\u{g}lu and Pavl\r{u} proved not to be CCZ-equivalent to permutations when $4$ divides $n$. With their result, our computations show that this holds for every even $n\le 24$. In dimension $18$ the necessary condition is satisfied, and the new test decides the case. We conjecture this for every even dimension. We also compile $25$ classes of quadratic APN functions in dimension ten from published instances, with equivalence certificates. No function in these classes or in their switching closure is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation. All code and data are public.
item.dc:creator: Emanuele Bellini

item.title: Mobility Information Capacity of Multi-Robot Systems: Safety-Aware Maneuver Design
item.description: arXiv:2611.10298v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multiple robots operating in shared workspaces must adjust their speed, direction, and trajectories to coordinate with one another and respond to changing tasks and disturbances. The available maneuver freedom depends on the dynamics, uncertainty, and safety margins, even for a fixed fleet size and workspace. However, robot count, workspace occupancy, and task throughput do not quantify how much the fleet can vary its motion or how reliably these variations can be observed. We develop a mobility information capacity (MIC) framework that jointly characterizes these two aspects. Mobility information is defined as the mutual information between a joint maneuver sequence and its noisy trajectory observation, and MIC maximizes this quantity under maneuver-resource constraints. For a linear Gaussian maneuver-to-observation model with feedback dynamics, we characterize the finite-horizon information benchmark and derive its stationary long-horizon spectral limit, accounting for heterogeneous mobility gains, colored uncertainty, and temporally coupled maneuver costs. We further map workspace-boundary, inter-robot separation, and actuator chance constraints into coupled maneuver-covariance restrictions and derive conditions under which covariance optimization reduces to resource allocation across mobility modes. Finite joint maneuver codebooks are then constructed through individual risk screening and noise-whitened trajectory separation, with bounds linking sequence recovery error and achieved information to the capacity benchmarks. An aerial-robot simulation study evaluates spectral convergence, safety-aware allocation, finite-codebook identification, and fleet-size scaling. The resulting framework complements occupancy and task-throughput measures by quantifying the maximum observable maneuver freedom supported by a mobility system.
item.dc:creator: Weijie Yuan

item.title: Analysis of the Effect of Doppler on Direct-to-Cell: Real-World Performance and Proposed Improvements
item.description: arXiv:2611.11065v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Direct-to-cell (DtC) satellites serve unmodified LTE phones today from low Earth orbit, where the satellite's motion creates Doppler shifts of tens of kHz. Since large offsets such as these cannot be compensated adequately by the user equipment (UE), the satellite pre-compensates the Doppler shift of each beam, but it can do so for only one reference point in the beam. A UE elsewhere in the beam still has to compensate a residual offset; previous field studies report residuals of up to 10 kHz, beyond the $\pm$7.5 kHz that the 15 kHz subcarrier spacing can resolve. In this paper we corroborate this effect with our own detailed measurements of Starlink transmissions and further correlate ineffective handover performance to inadequate residual offset compensation. We analyze the Doppler compensation problem with detailed standard-specific simulations and propose a compensation method at the UE, based on the location of the UE with respect to the beam reference point used for the Doppler compensation and the known satellite location, that improves the efficiency of handover. With UE cell-specific pre-compensation, the neighbors are identified, read correctly and handed over to in time rather than lost to radio-link failure.
item.dc:creator: Yuxi Chen, Muhammad Iqbal Rochman, Kyler McCormack, Jakob Kotz, Monisha Ghosh

item.title: Linear Set Reconciliation with $O(d)$ Additive Redundancy
item.description: arXiv:2611.11409v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In set reconciliation, two parties holding sets $A, B \subseteq [n]$ with $|A \triangle B| \le d$ seek to recover their symmetric difference from short $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear sketches, which is equivalent to recovering a $d$-sparse vector $x = \mathbf{1}_{A \triangle B} \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ from its syndrome $Hx \in \mathbb{F}_2^m$. While the information-theoretic counting bound requires $L(n,d) := \log \sum_{i=0}^d \binom{n}{i} = d\log(n/d) + \Theta(d)$ bits, existing polynomial-time schemes either use at least $d\lceil\log(n+1)\rceil$ bits (algebraic sketches, leaving an $\Omega(d\log d)$-bit gap) or incur a multiplicative $(1+\delta)L(n,d)$ overhead (peeling-based sketches), raising the question of whether $L(n,d) + O(d)$ bits is achievable with fast updates and decoding. We construct a public-coin randomized $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear sketch of length $L(n,d) + O(d) + \lambda\log^{O(1)} n$ that recovers each fixed input of weight at most $d$ with probability at least $1 - 2^{-\lambda}$, with $\log^{O(1)} n$ update time and $d\exp(O((\log\log n)^2)) = dn^{o(1)}$ worst-case decoding time. In particular, for $n \le 2^{\operatorname{polylog}(d)}$ and $\lambda \le d^{1-\Omega(1)}$, this achieves $L(n,d) + O(d)$ bits with $\operatorname{polylog}(d)$ update time and $d^{1+o(1)}$ decoding time. Our construction encodes $d$ permuted rows via randomly scaled Pinsketch syndromes and sketches the resulting bit array column by column. Decoding columns sequentially from prefix predictions cancels recovered rows and exposes undecided rows as decoder-side hints, reducing each column to a hinted sparse recovery problem that we solve via a recursive sketch, HintSketch.
item.dc:creator: Tianren Liu, Rui Xu, Tong Yang, Kangyang Zhou

item.title: CHANNELS4WORLD: An Environment-Scale Dataset for Wireless Foundation Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.11428v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wireless foundation models learn reusable representations across tasks, configurations, and deployment environments. Their pretraining requires environmental breadth, yet wireless datasets often sample few sites densely. We introduce Channels4World, a scene-centered dataset of 100,000 distinct outdoor RF scenes and a procedural method for generating them. Each scene links a generated environment and RF material assignments to 32 base-station (BS) positions, 16,384 UE positions, and aligned variable-length multipath and ordered interaction records at 3.5 and 7~GHz. The corpus comprises 52.43 billion physical BS-UE pairs, 104.86 billion frequency-specific evaluations, and a 29.14-TB packaged payload. Scene identity aligns geometry, placements, channels, and interactions across frequencies, allowing environmental breadth and within-scene observation density to vary independently. The public release offers predefined subsets at multiple scales and separate access to corpus components. A deterministic 90K/10K scene-level train-test split keeps both frequencies and all scene components together. We characterize morphology, RF materials, and transceiver placement across three generation profiles. Controlled propagation and path-retention analyses show that diffraction materially affects retained-link availability and multipath structure, while the retention policy reduces storage substantially with little loss in represented aggregate power. Under matched training exposure, models trained on broader scene collections perform better on held-out scenes, although an equal-episode control shows that scene count alone cannot explain the gain. By making environmental breadth explicit and controllable, Channels4World supports the development and evaluation of wireless foundation models for generalization across deployment environments.
item.dc:creator: Joonkyu Jang, Hyung-Joo Moon, Kwang Soon Kim, Seong-Lyun Kim, Jakob Hoydis, Robert W. Heath, Jr., Chan-Byoung Chae

item.title: Karhunen-Lo\`eve Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.11624v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Karhunen-Lo\`eve transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix with computable bounds: for the $8\times8$ Markov block of image coding at pole $0.95$ it is below 1.2 percent. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra; a moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exact for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows; the dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means.
item.dc:creator: Mitchell A. Thornton

item.title: Identifiable but Hard to Estimate: Rotation in Equally Spaced Overcomplete ICA
item.description: arXiv:2611.11852v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How many observations are needed to estimate a common rotation in two-dimensional overcomplete independent component analysis? We study equally spaced mixing columns with known source count, common source law, and column norm. For a fixed non-Gaussian fourth-order Gram-Charlier source law, the rotation is identifiable modulo the column spacing. Yet the sample size for fixed relative angular accuracy grows exponentially with the source count. We characterize this sample size, up to absolute constants, by the reciprocal of the squared Hellinger distance between two rotations separated by half the column spacing. An explicit radially weighted phase estimator attains this scale uniformly over the rotation family, using the observation radius to prevent cancellation in the mean of an angular harmonic. We also determine the exact exponential decay rate of single-observation total variation for the same pair. This gives bounds on the sample size exponent; its exact value remains open. Finally, a noisy binary-source example shows how an exact zero line of the observed characteristic function can have an exponentially small normal derivative.
item.dc:creator: Wenjun Xiao, Yinghao Fang, Hanxin Chen, Sihan Jia, Vince D Calhoun, Yuda BI

item.title: Polynomial Sample Complexity of Noninteractive Simulation over Finite Alphabets
item.description: arXiv:2611.11974v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study noninteractive simulation from a finite correlated source. Alice and Bob observe independent copies of the source and generate outputs without communication. We give a quantitative construction for arbitrary finite output alphabets: for every fixed source, a joint law that is simulable with arbitrarily many samples can be approximated using a number of samples polynomial jointly in the output alphabet sizes and the inverse accuracy. We first study binary outputs. A one-sided Wright--Fisher comparison gives a source-dependent explicit exponent and a finite-head Gaussian-threshold representation. We then handle arbitrary finite output alphabets through averaged influence regularity, simplex-preserving Gaussian moment lifting, and a common Gaussian projection for all correlated-prefix states. The sample exponent is independent of the output alphabet sizes. For a concrete biased binary source we certify an explicit exponent below $19$.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Wang

item.title: An Explicit Below Half Threshold Bound for the Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir's Secret Sharing Scheme
item.description: arXiv:2611.12325v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As a fundamental cryptographic primitive, secret sharing distributes a secret among multiple parties and allows certain authorized parties to recover the secret while preventing unauthorized parties from knowing the secret. However, local leakage from each party member allows an adversary to learn partial information from each share, which is not guaranteed by traditional security. In this paper, we study bounds on the reconstruction threshold of Shamir's secret sharing scheme over prime fields against arbitrary 1-bit local leakage. We show that, for all sufficiently large $n$ and every prime $p>n$, the $(n,t)$-Shamir's scheme is $\exp(-\Omega(n))$-resilient whenever $t/n\geq 0.489$, for any choice of distinct nonzero evaluation points. Our proof refines the dual-code list recovery analysis and combines complementary Fourier estimates according to the support sizes and biases of the leakage functions, yielding an improved explicit reconstruction threshold bound.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Zhang, Xin Wang, Xiangliang Kong

item.title: Quantum Robustness via Sandwiched R\'enyi Divergences
item.description: arXiv:2611.12738v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: If a quantum state is known only approximately, how much can the expectation of an observable change? We answer with the worst-case expectation over all states within a sandwiched R\'enyi divergence budget of a reference state, for every order $\alpha \in [1/2,\infty]$. Convex duality gives this value as a one-dimensional optimization over a sandwiched Schatten norm, running from a fidelity risk at $\alpha = 1/2$, through the entropic risk at $\alpha = 1$, to a quantum conditional value-at-risk at $\alpha = \infty$. The main result is a classicalization theorem: the quantum problem coincides with the classical one for a probability measure $\omega_\alpha$ on the spectral interval of the observable, constructed from Hein\"avaara's tracial joint spectral measure and given by Stahl's theorem at $\alpha = 1$. The Hoeffding, Bernstein and Markov--Krein bounds of classical probability thereby apply to the quantum problem, and yield Pinsker-type inequalities with Bernstein-type refinements. The measure $\omega_\alpha$ is the Born measure only at $\alpha = 1/2$; for $\alpha > 1/2$, noncommutativity of the observable with the state strictly lowers its variance below the Born variance, and with it every variance-sensitive bound: a quantum deflation.
item.dc:creator: Luc Rey-Bellet

item.title: A Spectral Representation Of The Simple Hypothesis Testing Problem
item.description: arXiv:2601.09564v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The minimum Type II error probability (or volume) of simple hypothesis tests with randomized detectors is expressed as a Riemann integral of the (cumulative) distribution function of the likelihood ratio for all non-negative Type I error probability (or volume) values: $\beta(\varepsilon)=\int_{0}^{\infty}|F(1/\tau)-\varepsilon|^{+}d\tau$ for all $\varepsilon\geq0$. The derivation relies on convex conjugation (the Legendre transform) and level set integration, and is sufficiently general to extend to tests between $\sigma$-finite measures. Measure change identities relating the $\beta(\cdot)$ functions of different hypothesis testing problems are established. Approximations for Type II and Type I volumes are derived under two different hypotheses concerning the Kolmogorov distance to normality for the log-likelihood ratio distributions. In both the Central Limit Theorem and the large deviations regimes, the resulting non-asymptotic expressions recover and extend state-of-the-art characterizations of optimal performance in the memoryless case, and improve and generalize them in the Markovian case. Finally, The distinction between the implications of the Central Limit Theorem and the Berry--Esseen Theorem for the asymptotic simple hypothesis testing problem is clarified.
item.dc:creator: Bar{\i}\c{s} Nakibo\u{g}lu

item.title: DNA-MGC+: A versatile codec for reliable and resource-efficient data storage on synthetic DNA
item.description: arXiv:2603.14527v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The biochemical processes underlying DNA data storage, including synthesis, amplification, and sequencing, are inherently noisy, leading to insertion, deletion, and substitution errors as well as sequence dropouts that challenge reliable data retrieval. Here we introduce DNA-MGC+, a DNA storage codec designed for reliable and resource-efficient retrieval under diverse operating conditions. We evaluate DNA-MGC+ across various in silico and in vitro settings. In comparison with selected representative codecs, the results show that DNA-MGC+ consistently improves key performance metrics under explicit reliability constraints, including required sequencing depth, read cost, decoding time, storage density, and error-correction capability. In silico experiments show that DNA-MGC+ supports reliable decoding at error rates up to 24% for a 15-KB file, while separate scalability experiments demonstrate reliable decoding of files up to 200 MB at a 5% error rate. In vitro experiments involving a 24-KB file and electrochemical synthesis show that different DNA-MGC+ configurations achieve minimum sequencing depths below 3x and read costs below 3.5 nts/bit under both Illumina and Nanopore sequencing.
item.dc:creator: Ramy Khabbaz, J\'er\'emy Mateos, Marc Antonini, Serge Kas Hanna

item.title: CL-SEC: Cross-Layer Semantic Error Correction Empowered by Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2603.26125v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Achieving reliable communication has long been a fundamental challenge in networked systems. Semantic Error Correction (SEC) leverages the semantic understanding capabilities of language models (LMs) to perform application-layer error correction, complementing conventional channel decoding. While promising, existing SEC approaches rely solely on context captured by LMs at the application layer, ignoring the rich information available at the physical layer. To address this limitation, this paper introduces Cross-Layer SEC (CL-SEC), an LM-empowered error correction framework that integrates cross-layer information from both the physical and application layers to jointly correct corrupted words in text communication. Using a Bayesian combination in product form tailored to this framework, CL-SEC achieves significantly improved performance over methods that process information in isolated layers. CL-SEC shows substantial gains across multiple error-correction metrics, including bit-error rate, word-error rate, and semantic fidelity scores. Importantly, unlike most semantic communication systems that focus solely on recovering the semantic meaning of transmitted messages, CL-SEC aims to reconstruct the original transmitted message verbatim, leveraging the semantic understanding capabilities of LMs for precise reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Yirun Wang, Yuyang Du, Soung Chang Liew, Yuchen Pan, Feifan Zhang, Lihao Zhang

item.title: Design and Analysis of Quantum Dual-Containing CSS LDPC Codes based on Quasi-Dyadic Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2605.03631v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum error correcting codes are essential to achieve fault-tolerant quantum computation. This work introduces two constructions of high-rate, dual-containing (DC) Calderbank--Shor--Steane low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes based on quasi-dyadic matrices. We characterize the automorphism group of such codes, investigate their minimum distance behavior, and provide several theoretical results on their cycle properties. Monte Carlo simulations under depolarizing and phenomenological noise show better finite-length logical error rates than the considered DC benchmark codes and competitive performance against several state-of-the-art quantum LDPC code families. Finally, we employ an automorphism-ensemble belief propagation decoder to improve their decoding performance.
item.dc:creator: Alessio Baldelli, Marco Baldi, Massimo Battaglioni, Franco Chiaraluce, Paolo Santini

item.title: Constructions of locally repairable codes via concatenated codes
item.description: arXiv:2605.04618v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Locally repairable codes (LRCs) have attracted considerable attention owing to their pivotal role in distributed storage systems. Since binary linear LRCs can significantly reduce the complexity of both encoding and decoding, the construction of binary LRCs has drawn extensive research interest. In this paper, we construct binary LRCs with locality $r=2$ and disjoint local repair groups via classical concatenation, where the outer codes are linear codes over $\mathbb{F}_4$ and the inner code is the binary $[3,2,2]$ linear code. We present a systematic approach for selecting outer codes to obtain LRCs attaining specified bounds, and show that the weight distributions of the resulting binary LRCs are determined by those of the selected outer codes. Under certain sufficient conditions, we construct several classes of optimal binary LRCs, including those attaining Griesmer-type bounds and binary perfect LRCs. Furthermore, we sharpen the Johnson-like bounds of Ma and Ge for binary LRCs with locality $r=2$ and disjoint local repair groups, and define nearly perfect binary LRCs and $k$-optimal binary LRCs with respect to the improved bounds. We show that nearly perfect binary LRCs can be constructed via concatenation when the outer codes are nearly perfect linear codes over $\mathbb{F}_4$. Finally, we present several examples of such nearly perfect and $k$-optimal binary LRCs.
item.dc:creator: Hengfeng Jin, Fang-Wei Fu

item.title: List Recovery for Random Low-Rate Linear Codes
item.description: arXiv:2605.30101v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that random linear codes of fixed dimension $d$ over sufficiently large prime fields have nearly optimal output list size for list recovery. Fix an error fraction $0<\alpha<1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$. For all sufficiently large block lengths $n$, with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$, the following holds simultaneously for every input list size $\ell\le 2^{\delta n/\log n}$, where $\delta>0$ depends only on $\alpha,\varepsilon$, and $d$. Given any list of $\ell$ symbols at each coordinate, at most $(1+\varepsilon)\ell/(1-\alpha)$ codewords agree with the lists in at least $(1-\alpha)n$ coordinates. Our proof adapts the colored-graph and determinant arguments of Matousek, Privetivy, and Skovron for reconstructing planar point sets from their projections. We also prove that the range of input list sizes is nearly optimal. There is a constant $c=c(\alpha,\varepsilon)>0$ such that, for every linear code of dimension at least two over a sufficiently large prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$ and every $2^{cn}\le\ell\le p$, there are lists of size $\ell$ and a set of more than $(1+\varepsilon)\ell/(1-\alpha)$ codewords, each of which agrees with those lists in every coordinate. The main results of this paper were discovered by ChatGPT 5.5 Sol using harness components from the UCLA Moonshot Harness Project, in response to a less optimal result found by the authors. See the end of the introduction for a discussion.
item.dc:creator: Isaac M Hair, Amit Sahai

item.title: Coding for Multiple Reverse-Complement and Palindromic Duplications
item.description: arXiv:2609.00779v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reverse-complement (RC) and palindromic (PAL) duplications insert a reversed copy of a length-$k$ block immediately after the block; an RC duplication also applies a fixed involutive complement to the inserted symbols. We study $q$-ary codes correcting $t$ such operations applied in sequence, where later operations may copy inserted symbols. For fixed $q\geq2$ and $k,t\geq1$, we prove that every length-$n$ code $C$ for either channel has redundancy $n-\log_q|C|\geq t\log_q n-O_{q,k,t}(1)$; for fixed $q,k$ and $1\leq t=t(n)=o(n)$ the lower bound is $t\log_q(n/t)-O_{q,k}(t)$. For fixed $k$, known codes for one length-$k$ insertion burst attain redundancy $\log_q n+O_{q,k}(1)$ for a single duplication of either type. For every even $k$ and any involutive complement, we show that the two channels are equivalent for every number of errors: the bijection complementing every other coordinate turns each RC duplication into a PAL duplication. This bijection therefore converts any $t$-error-correcting RC code into a PAL code of the same size, and conversely, with linear-time transfer of encoders and decoders. For every even $k$, we also determine the maximum number of descendants of one word under exactly two errors; by the bijection, it is the same for both channels. For fixed even $k$, a direct count using this maximum proves the existence of two-error-correcting PAL and RC codes with redundancy at most $4\log_q n+O_{q,k}(1)$. A known existence bound for two deletion bursts transfers to insertions with the same leading term as ours and a larger additive constant. For two errors, the converse gives $2\log_q n-O_{q,k}(1)$, a factor of two below these existence bounds.
item.dc:creator: Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy (Yohananov)

item.title: Double circulant LCD codes over $\mathbb{F}_2+u\mathbb{F}_2$ and their related binary LCD codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.16121v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes are linear codes that intersect their dual trivially. We study double circulant (Euclidean) LCD codes over the finite chain ring $R=\mathbb F_2+u\mathbb F_2$, where $u^2=0$. Using the Chinese Remainder Theorem and the factorization of $x^n-1$, we derive an explicit enumeration formula, with a separate treatment of the constituent corresponding to $x-1$, which is not obtained by a formal specialization of the previously known counting formula over $\mathbb F_q[u]/(u^k)$. Assuming Artin's primitive root conjecture for $2$, we show that the binary Gray images contain an asymptotically good family of rate $1/2$ which attains the asymptotic Gilbert--Varshamov bound, i.e., whose relative distance can approach $H_2^{-1}(1/2)$ from below. More importantly from the constructive viewpoint, by combining Gray images with a known extension construction, we obtain a binary LCD code with previously unknown parameters $[29,15,7]$ and construct two explicit permutation-inequivalent binary LCD codes with parameters $[45,23,9]$ and nine binary LCD codes with the best known parameters.
item.dc:creator: Xingxing Xu, Bo Wu, Jon-Lark Kim

item.title: LWM-TF: A Wireless Foundation Model on 5G NR Time-Frequency Resource Grids
item.description: arXiv:2610.21013v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. Without any impairment labels, distances in the frozen feature space flag unseen waveform impairments with 0.78 macro AUROC, against 0.68 for receiver statistics. A single pre-trained encoder thus provides receiver features that transfer across tasks, most strongly when labels are scarce.
item.dc:creator: Namhyun Kim, Sadjad Alikhani, Ahmed Alkhateeb

item.title: Beyond Typical Strings: Sampling the Complexity Landscape
item.description: arXiv:2611.00162v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Uniform random sampling of strings is overwhelmingly dominated by high-complexity strings, leaving the much smaller set of low- and intermediate-complexity strings largely unexplored. Here, we adapt the nested neutral set estimator (NNSE), a Monte Carlo rare-event sampling method, to estimate the distribution P(K) of complexity values for binary strings of fixed length. NNSE allows us to explore the full complexity landscape, including exponentially rare low-complexity regions that are inaccessible to direct sampling, for string lengths up to several hundred. We apply the method to several widely used complexity measures: Lempel-Ziv 76 (LZ76), Lempel-Ziv 78 (LZ78), context tree weighting (CTW), the block decomposition method (BDM), and block entropy. We further introduce uniform complexity weighting (UCW), which gives equal weight to different complexity levels rather than to individual strings. Using NNSE to perform UCW sampling allows us to compare complexity measures across their full range in a dataset-independent way. This reveals differences in their behavior for low- and intermediate-complexity strings that are practically inaccessible to conventional uniform sampling.
item.dc:creator: Abdurrahman Hadi Erturk, Joshua Sharkey, Nora S Martin, Kamal Dingle, Ard A Louis

item.title: Common zeros of homogeneous polynomials and the weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.08203v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the maximum number of common zeros in projective space of any set of linearly independent homogeneous polynomials of the same degree, when the degree is smaller than the cardinality of the finite field. This proves the conjecture of Beelen, Datta, and Ghorpade, resolving a longstanding problem on common zeros and determining the complete weight hierarchy of the corresponding projective Reed-Muller codes. The proof uses Green's hyperplane restriction bound, combined with a footprint argument that reduces the problem to the affine case solved by Heijnen and Pellikaan. Wei duality then determines the hierarchy in sufficiently large degrees, recovering the complete hierarchy in every degree for the projective plane. Finally, we prove an upper bound valid in every degree, and conjecture that it is always sharp.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo San-Jos\'e

item.title: On the Monotonicity of Information Measures
item.description: arXiv:2404.15158v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the monotonicity of information measures, functions that assign a value to each statistical experiment, with respect to the Blackwell and Lehmann orders. We show that such monotonicity can be characterized by local, first-order conditions. Under natural invariance properties, a measure is Blackwell monotone if and only if it decreases in the direction of signal replacements, and Lehmann monotone if and only if it decreases in the direction of reverse signal replacements, which replace signals with higher ones only in low states or with lower ones only in high states. We translate both conditions into the space of posterior beliefs and apply them to likelihood-separable and posterior-separable measures, showing in particular that the entropy cost is Lehmann monotone. Among posterior-separable measures, we further identify a Lehmann monotone subclass, posterior-mean-ratio measures, that characterizes the Lehmann order.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyu Cheng, Yonggyun Kim

item.title: Sample-Efficient Quantum State Tomography for Structured Quantum States in One Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2410.02583v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we answer this fundamental question affirmatively by using a class of informationally complete positive operator-valued measures (IC-POVMs), including symmetric IC-POVMs (SIC-POVMs) and spherical $t$-designs, focusing on sample complexity while not accounting for the implementation complexity of the measurement settings. For SIC-POVMs and spherical 2-designs, we show that the number of state copies to guarantee bounded recovery error of an MPO state with a constrained least-squares estimator depends on the probability distribution of the MPO under the POVM but scales only linearly with $n$ when the distribution is approximately uniform. For general spherical $t$-designs with a sufficiently large $t$, we prove that only a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is sufficient for a guaranteed recovery of any state represented by an MPO. In addition, we establish a sample complexity lower bound based on the Cramer-Rao bound, showing that, for strictly positive definite MPO states and unbiased estimators, a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is also necessary, although the upper and lower bounds do not yet match in their dependence on the target accuracy. Furthermore, we propose a spectral method and a projected gradient descent (PGD) algorithm to solve the constrained least-squares problem, both equipped with rigorous recovery error guarantees.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Qin, Casey Jameson, Alireza Goldar, Michael B. Wakin, Zhexuan Gong, Zhihui Zhu

item.title: Neural Window Decoding of Spatially Coupled LDPC Codes: Exploiting Window Structure for Learning and Adaptation
item.description: arXiv:2411.19092v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a neural window decoder (NWD) for spatially coupled low-density parity-check (SC-LDPC) codes. The proposed methods adapt neural min-sum decoding to the structure and sequential operation of window decoding. First, target-oriented training restricts the loss to the variable nodes whose decisions are required at each window stage. Second, learned damping factors identify check-node updates that can reuse messages from the preceding iteration. Finally, adaptive weight switching selects weights trained for unreliable inherited information when a previous-window failure is detected. For a length-$20{,}000$ $(3,6)$-regular SC-LDPC code, the target-oriented NWD achieves performance comparable to sum-product window decoding while using min-sum updates. On the reduced target graph, scheduling based on regularized damping factors yields an estimated computational cost 48\% lower than that of full-graph weighted min-sum decoding, while maintaining comparable decoding performance. Adaptive weight switching improves decoding performance by 35\% at 3.0 dB relative to plain weights. These learning methods exploit the properties of window decoding to improve the reliability and computational efficiency of SC-LDPC convolutional codes.
item.dc:creator: Dae-Young Yun, Hee-Youl Kwak, Sang-Hyo Kim, Yongjune Kim, Jong-Seon No

item.title: A reverse entropy power inequality for i.i.d. log-concave random variables
item.description: arXiv:2510.09206v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that $h_\infty(X+Y)\leq h_\infty(Z+W)$, where $X, Y$ are independent log-concave random variables, and $Z, W$ are exponential random variables having the same respective $\infty$-R\'enyi entropies. Analogs for integer-valued monotone log-concave random variables are also obtained. Our main tools are decreasing rearrangement, majorization, and the change of measure.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Fu, Jiange Li

item.title: Laws of Learning Dynamics and the Core of Learners
item.description: arXiv:2602.05026v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We formulate an algorithm-independent theory of learning dynamics for individual models and ensembles. We establish a conservation law, the vanishing of predictive entropy under successful learning, quantitative entropy and core-expansion bounds, and calibration and finite-sample validation results for identifying reliable predictions. These results motivate a two-generation ensemble that uses Jensen-Shannon (JS) disagreement to route uncertain inputs to specialized learners. CIFAR-10 experiments examine controlled perturbations, distribution shifts, and adversarial attacks. On a heterogeneous test environment, routing improves accuracy over probability averaging while keeping core accuracy near 95%. For adversarial defense, we consider a query-only black-box setting: the attacker can query the overall prediction function but does not know a particular internal decomposition into learners and routing rules. Our current attacks use a fixed-initial-route gradient, which is accurate for a single-step attack when the route remains unchanged, but may deviate from actual multi-step attacks, especially for large perturbations. We evaluate our two-layer defense against this approximation; whether additional adversarially trained layers improve resistance to stronger multi-step attacks remains for future study.
item.dc:creator: Inkee Jung, Siu Cheong Lau

item.title: Efficient Soft-Output Guessing for Enhanced Quantum Tanner Code Decoding
item.description: arXiv:2603.18318v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a generalized low-density parity-check decoding framework for quantum Tanner codes utilizing soft-output guessing random additive noise decoding (SOGRAND). By soft-output decoding entire component codes rather than individual parity checks, we mitigate the effects of trapping sets and cycles, resulting in improved convergence. Because our decoder preserves the message passing structure of standard belief propagation (BP), it is compatible with many BP enhancements. We demonstrate this with OSD postprocessing, quaternary BP, and RelayBP, each yielding further gains. Standalone SOGRAND outperforms the standard BP+OSD baseline by over two orders of magnitude in logical error rate. In combination with the Relay principle, SOGRAND outperforms RelayBP by over one order of magnitude, providing a way forward for scalable decoding of the emerging class of Tanner-code-based quantum codes.
item.dc:creator: Lukas Rapp, Muriel M\'edard, Eugene Tang, Ken R. Duffy

item.title: Statistical Physics of Coding for the Integers
item.description: arXiv:2604.00858v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a paradigm of coding for compression of the natural numbers via the zeta distribution and develop a statistical-mechanical interpretation, both in terms of Hagedorn systems and a Bose gas with energy levels given by logarithms of prime numbers. We also propose a simple coding scheme for the zeta distribution that nearly achieves the ideal code length. For block coding of vectors of natural numbers, we derive the micro-canonical entropy function and demonstrate its asymptotic linearity implying that its behavior is analogous to that of a Hagedorn system. We also derive the large deviations rate function, and provide a formula for the best coding parameter in the large deviations sense. We show that due the Hagedorn-type phase transition there is only partial equivalence of ensembles, due to the degeneration of the domain of the partition function.
item.dc:creator: Neri Merhav

item.title: Amortized Vine Copulas for High-Dimensional Density and Information Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2604.20568v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Modeling high-dimensional dependencies while keeping likelihoods tractable re- mains challenging. Classical vine copulas provide an explicit dependence structure but require repeated, costly bivariate fitting. We propose Vine Denoising Copula (VDC)1, an amortized estimator for simplified vines on continuous data. VDC trains a single bivariate denoising network on simulated copulas and reuses it across all vine edges. For each edge, the network maps an empirical histogram to a density grid, and iterative proportional fitting approximately enforces uniform grid marginals. The predicted densities and cached conditional transforms support stan- dard vine recursion, likelihood evaluation, sampling, and information estimation.
